Association analysis between genes and/or metadata variables

rna_association.Rd

Computes pairwise associations between features derived from normalized RNA-seq expression data and/or sample metadata, returning both a structured result object and a heatmap-style visualization.

Usage

rna_association(
  project,
  x_features,
  y_features = NULL,
  x_type = c("auto", "gene", "metadata", "gsva"),
  y_type = c("auto", "gene", "metadata", "gsva"),
  format = "continuous",
  group = NULL,
  method = c("spearman", "pearson", "kendall"),
  compute_mi = FALSE,
  mi_method = c("knn", "discrete"),
  cluster = TRUE,
  save = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

x_features

Character vector of features to place on the x-axis. Features may represent genes or metadata variables depending on x_type.

y_features

Optional character vector of features to place on the y-axis. If NULL, uses x_features.

x_type

Character. Type of x-axis features. Currently supported: auto, gene, metadata and gsva.

y_type

Character. Type of y-axis features. Currently supported: auto, gene metadata and gsva.

format

Character. Data format expected for association analysis. Currently supports continuous.

group

Optional character. Restricts analysis to samples belonging to the specified group in metadata.

method

Correlation method used for association analysis. One of pearson, spearman, or kendall.

compute_mi

Logical. Whether to additionally compute mutual information for each association pair (default: FALSE).

mi_method

Method used for mutual information estimation. One of knn or discrete.

cluster

Logical. Whether to hierarchically cluster rows and columns when the association matrix is symmetric (default: TRUE).

save

Logical. Whether to store results in the active rna_project (default: TRUE).

verbose

Logical. Whether to display the association heatmap and print a summary object in the console (default: TRUE).

Value

Invisibly returns either:

  • the updated rna_project object when save = TRUE;

  • or an object of class rna_association when save = FALSE.

The rna_association object contains:

matrix

Association matrix.

long

Long-format association table containing correlation coefficients and p-values.

plot

Generated ggplot2 heatmap object.

x_features

Features used on the x-axis.

y_features

Features used on the y-axis.

x_type

Type of x-axis features.

y_type

Type of y-axis features.

params

List containing analysis parameters and metadata.

Details

The function currently supports continuous variables using correlation-based association metrics and is designed to be extensible to future multi-omics and mixed-data analyses.

The function was designed as a generalized association engine capable of integrating transcriptomic and metadata-derived variables within a unified framework.

Currently, associations are computed using correlation-based statistics applied to continuous variables.

Gene identifiers may be provided either as gene symbols or Ensembl IDs, provided that annotation information is available in the project object.

When cluster = TRUE and the matrix is symmetric, hierarchical clustering is applied using:

  • distance: 1 - correlation

  • linkage: complete linkage clustering

If compute_mi = TRUE, mutual information values are additionally estimated for each feature pair using either:

  • discretization-based estimation;

  • K-nearest neighbors estimation.

The resulting heatmap is generated using ggplot2.

Significant associations (p < 0.05) are marked with asterisks.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

# Gene-gene association matrix
rna_association(
  project = my_project,
  x_features = c("SERTAD3", "MFSD4B", "RNF139")
)

# Metadata vs genes
rna_association(
  project = my_project,
  x_features = c("Age", "BMI"),
  y_features = c("IL7R", "GZMB"),
  x_type = "metadata",
  y_type = "gene"
)

# Spearman correlation with MI
rna_association(
  project = my_project,
  x_features = c("GeneA", "GeneB"),
  method = "spearman",
  compute_mi = TRUE
)

# Restrict analysis to one group
rna_association(
  project = my_project,
  x_features = c("GeneA", "GeneB"),
  group = "Control"
)
} # }
